count_claim: Expected anchor_mapping_count under the staged fix on the best-known (igf3/launch-9) shape = 7 (1 exec + 6 readable + 0 prot-0/other). Margin vs cap 8 = 1 slot. Any single additional fragment (LOAD8 materializing as 1 record -> exactly 8, zero margin; 2 records -> 9) silently drops record #7 [0x970c000,0x9a34000) — the GUA-hosting, highest, most load-bearing span (first-come ascending-address cap semantics).

recommendation.one_liner:
-static constexpr size_t kMaxAnchorMappings = 8;
+static constexpr size_t kMaxAnchorMappings = 16;
recommendation.rationale: observed 7 with zero slack after ONE extra fragment; worst pinned fragmentation behavior (LOAD7 -> 4 records) plus LOAD8 materialization plus RELRO splits plus a guard/reservation plausibly reaches 11-14; 16 covers it; cost = +8 slots x 20B (24B padded) ~= +192B in an in-process snapshot that already carries a 1024-entry mapping array (~20KB); the collection loop bound (line 483) and the adapter's count-bounded iteration need no change; all consumers (bridge PRX, entry PRX, core TU, adapter TU, fixtures) compile the single shared header, and the raw snapshot never crosses a module boundary (conversion happens in-process), so no ABI skew; saturation remains visible via lmf_anchor_count==16
recommendation.fallback_if_not_folded: shipping cap=8 is acceptable-but-fragile: conversion REFUSAL risk stays low (all 6 readable records rank in the first 8 under any plausible shape, so the D2 filter keeps >=1 readable span); the realistic failure is silent loss of the top RW span -> stage-2 GUA reads land outside declared ranges -> readpath-guard/required-slot degradation (deterministic, memory-safe), NOT a crash

limits: The igf3 clean walk is a 2026-10-04 boot; the launch-9 boot (2026-10-05) is pinned only by the COUNT 6 (readable, intersecting), not by an itemized span list — the launch-9 registration logs counters only.
The task brief's extent [0x400000,0xfc602c8) matches the r11-era clamp comment, not the r13/fix constants ([0x400000,0xc0602c8)); on pinned evidence both give the same 7-record count.
No observation pins whether LOAD8 (---, 40MB) can materialize as records on some boot; its materialization is the most plausible +1/+2 fragmentation source.
